rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah sequence answers Quraysh: al-Kahf addresses two questions, al-Isrāʾ a third, and Maryam exposes older prophetic history and religious decline after the prophets.
rows.anchor: جاءت سورة مريم كاشفة - تبكيتا لأهل الكتاب الكاتمين للحق - عن أغرب من تلك القصص زأقدم زمانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This ordered response proves the Qurʾān is God’s speech: the Prophet’s reason and resolve would have let him answer the next day if he had composed it himself.
rows.anchor: ثبت بذلك أن هذا كله مرتب لإجابة سؤالهم وأنه كلام الله قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God left the question of the Spirit open and delayed the answer for no incapacity or ignorance; accounts of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the births of Jesus and Isaac show complete power and knowledge, and the reports fit reality.
rows.anchor: ما أجمل أمر الروح ولا أخر الإجابة خمس عشرة ليلة أو أقل أو أكثر من عجز ولا جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi connects the verse to the Prophet telling Gabriel that he had delayed so long that the Prophet suspected him; he says similar circumstances are mentioned in revelation reports.
rows.anchor: عن قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبرئيل عليه الصلاة والسلام ( لقد أبطات علي يا جبرئيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address calls God the Prophet’s beneficent Lord to honor and reassure him, explaining that both precedence and delay occur by divine command.
rows.anchor: ووقع الخطاب مقترنا بالوصف المفهم لمزيد الإكرام تطييبا لقلبه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tanazzul suggests honored, repeated descent at intervals; punishment instead requires command and arrives in the blink of an eye.
rows.anchor: ولفظ التنزل مشير إلى الإكرام , وهو التردد مرة بعد مرة ووقتا غب وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following resurrection with Paradise continues the pattern of mentioning Paradise after resurrection.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا عقب ذكر القيامة بذكر الجنة كما كان المعطوف عليه عقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the link seems distant, the verse answers objectors who might demand every account of the ancients: earlier and future reports come only by the Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: بأخبار هؤلاء إلا بأمر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies before and behind the angels and between it includes place, time, their own location, and what is above and below; they know and act accordingly, without acting in God’s dominion except by permission.
rows.anchor: أي من المكان والزمان وما فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is never forgetful of anything, so neither the Spirit’s details nor the Prophet’s needs escaped him and no revelation delay arose from ignorance.
rows.anchor: ولا ينسى ما يصلحك فيحتاج إلى مذكر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifteen-night-or-more delay could look like forgetfulness to the foolish, but God continuously observes the angels and directs their work at the wise, appointed time.
rows.anchor: فكان ذلك موهما للأغبياء أنه نسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form nasiy denies even occasional forgetfulness: a servant could be absent without leave only if his master were prone to prolonged lapses.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يتمكن العبد من الغيبة عن السيد بغير إذنه إلا أن كان بحيث يمكن أن يغفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah denies error and forgetfulness in language suited to its context, while affirming the required doctrine that God forgets nothing.
rows.anchor: فأتى في كل أسلوب بما يناسبه مع الوفاء بما يجب من حق الإعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together with the Qurʾān’s truthful descent and challenge, this verse forms a guard around the answers, turning away objections from every direction.
rows.anchor: لتكون الآيات رابطة على هذه الأجوبة وتوابعها وضابطة لها كالشهب والحرس الشديد بالنسبة إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God’s command and encompassing knowledge, the text names him Lord of the heavens, earth, and all beings between them, making the case for resurrection more explicit and comprehensive.
rows.anchor: ولما وصف سبحانه وتعالى بنفوذ الأمر واتساع العلم على وجه ثبت به ما أخبر به عن الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God with continual vigilance and endure its demands with full effort, since worship entails severe striving.
rows.anchor: أي اصبر صبرا عظيما بغاية جهدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samiy means one truly sharing any divine attribute or even bearing God’s name; the rhetorical question argues that he has no counterpart.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا مماثل له حتى ولا في مجرد الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previously recounted questions and examples show God’s complete knowledge and power, especially in creating humans from dust, from parents, and from a woman without a man; denying resurrection despite such evidence is astonishing.
rows.anchor: شمول علمه وتمام قدرته لاسيما في إيجاد البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb marks renewed, repeated denial after evidence has made belief in resurrection necessary; a generic singular indicts the whole class, since reproving one entails reproving many.
rows.anchor: بلفظ المضارع المؤذن بالتجدد بعد هذا البيان المقتضي حتما لاعتقاده البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although endowed with reason and signs, people become absorbed in themselves and fail to contemplate their Lord’s perfection, then deem life after death implausible.
rows.anchor: فشغله الإنس بنفسه عن التأمل في كمال ربه منكرا مستبعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic future describes being brought out alive after a long sleep and scattered remains; the verb governing idha is a verb with the meaning of brought out, since the initial lam prevents idha from governing it.
rows.anchor: لمنع لام الابتداء لعمله فيما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim read yadhakkaru with a still dhāl, suggesting that even a slight recollection would guide the person to truth.
rows.anchor: بإسكال الذال على قراءة نافع وابن عامر وعاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers pronounce the dhāl and kāf open and doubled; Biqaʿi says a person sunk in heedlessness needs strenuous reflection.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الباقين بفتح الذال والكاف وتشديدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From before means before this dispute; deleting the nūn in yak makes the expression itself portray the human’s original nonexistence, from which God can recreate him.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقام لتحقيره بكونه عدما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the Prophet’s beneficent Lord and uses the majestic plural to announce resurrection and gathering, answering the disbeliever’s denial with a threat.
rows.anchor: مجيبا عن إنكاره مؤذنا بالغضب عليهم بالإعراض عنهم مخاطبا لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم تفخيما لشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person is gathered with the devil who led him, in chains, and then brought around deep, constricted Hell after a long wait.
rows.anchor: بجعل كل واحد منهم مع قرينه الذي أضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They kneel in terror and abasement, poised to obey commands at the dreadful sight.
rows.anchor: على الركب من هول المطلع وشدة الذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazʿ means to seize harshly and violently; shīʿa is a faction bound by a shared doctrine, from which the most obstinate are extracted.
rows.anchor: أي لنأخذن أخذا بشدة وعنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The selection exposes their insignificance and shows that divine mercy does not exclude majesty, pride, sovereignty, and retribution.
rows.anchor: مع صفة الرحمة التي غمرهم إحسانها وبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who most deserves Hell and each of its levels, so no one is placed in an undeserved rank; the majestic phrasing heightens the warning.
rows.anchor: فلا يظن بنا أنا نضع أحدا في غير دركته أو غير طبقته من دركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated thumma may mark temporal order, or the third knowing may stand for consigning each person to Hell according to his deserved punishment because God knows his crime and can punish.
rows.anchor: لأن من علم ذنب عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts to all people: everyone must enter Hell, and this entry is an unavoidable decree.
rows.anchor: أي وما { منكم } أيها الناس أحد { إلا واردها }

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says in al-Lawāmiʿ that all believers except prophets bear some bad trait and attain true felicity only after purification, which occurs through the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : ما من مؤمن - إلا الأنبياء -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word then signals that rescue seems remote; the majority reading means a great deliverance, while al-Kisāʾī’s reading means rescue without that added force, fitting differing human states.
rows.anchor: أي تنجية عظيمة على قراءة الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are rescued with Hell cool and safe for them when they pass through it, while persistent wrongdoers remain kneeling in the worst state, unable to find a way out.
rows.anchor: بأن تكون عليهم حال الورود بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are clear, whether intrinsically decisive or explained by decisive verses or the Prophet; their status is either emphatic or explanatory.
rows.anchor: أو متشابهات قد تبعها البيان بالمحكمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than assess the proofs, disbelievers use worldly abundance to taunt believers about which side has the better residence and assembly; they mistake prosperity for divine approval and ignore God’s power to remove it.
rows.anchor: وهي المفاخرة بالمكاثرة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqām with a ḍamma, meaning a place of standing or assembly, while the other readers use a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: على قراءة ابن كثير بضم الميم والجماعة بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unprefixed before signals that all earlier generations enjoyed better circumstances; the audience saw their homes and traces, and they had finer furnishings and appearance.
rows.anchor: لم يأت بالجار إعلاما بأن المتقدمين كلهم كانوا أرغد عيشا وأمكن حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly luxury does not prove a good afterlife: God’s established practice is to extend apparent ease to the deeply misguided, increasing their error through pleasures and long life spent in grave sins.
rows.anchor: مثلكم كونا راسخا بسط له في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command form falyamdud, with its lam, presents the extension as already carried out, as if the commanded event were certain.
rows.anchor: إيذانا بوجوده وجود المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extension continues until they see what God promised: either worldly punishment at believers’ or others’ hands, punishment in the grave, or the Hour and its unmatched terrors.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا بأيدي المؤمنين أو غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then they will know who has the worse place and weaker force; the wording answers their boasts about residence and assembly, using army because their aim is rivalry and not everyone in an assembly fights.
rows.anchor: وكأنه عبر بالجند لأن قصدهم المغالبة وما كل من في الندي يكون مقاتلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guided people gain guidance in place of the worldly ease withheld for their honor, while the misguided gain error through their worldly gifts; this is an instance of ellipsis by reciprocal implication.
rows.anchor: ذكر السعة بالمد للضال أولا دليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abiding good works are acts of obedience and knowledge that illuminate hearts, remain unspoiled by sin, and lead to God; they surpass unbelievers’ worldly gifts in reward and final outcome.
rows.anchor: من الطاعات والمعارف التي شرحت لها الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afaraʾayta uses seeing for comprehensive knowledge and reliable report, introducing a rebuke of the person who rejects the Day after its terrifying consequences were described.
rows.anchor: عن طلب الخير بالرؤية التي هي الطريق إلى الإحاطة بالأشياء علما وخبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier audaciously claims he will receive great wealth and children in the Hereafter, first disempowering the All-Powerful and then empowering a powerless creature.
rows.anchor: فلم يكفه في جهله تعجيز القادر حتى ضم إليه إقدار العاجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His claim would require either access to the unseen, which is beyond creatures, or a covenant with the Merciful earned through proper obedience; he has neither.
rows.anchor: الذي هو غائب عن كل مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects both supposed grounds, the promised wealth and children, and tells him to abandon the claim in humiliation.
rows.anchor: لم يقع شيء من هذين الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will preserve the claim for later reproach and punishment; alternatively, the future tense allows time for repentance before the record is made, an expression of general mercy.
rows.anchor: والإعلام بذلك للحث على التوبة قبل الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His punishment is extended through gradual causes: beloved wealth and children burden him with labor and disputes and deepen the unbelief that entails punishment after death.
rows.anchor: باستدراجه بأسبابه من كثرة النعم من الأموال والأولاد المحببة له في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death God inherits all the wealth and children the man claimed; he arrives alone after resurrection, powerless and stripped of honor and strength.
rows.anchor: مسكينا منعزلا عن كل شيء لا قدرة له على مال ولا ولد

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports that Khabbāb, a smith, sought payment for a sword from al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who demanded that he disbelieve in Muhammad; al-ʿĀṣ then claimed he would be resurrected wealthy with children and repay him, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال : كنت قينا بمكة فعملت للعاص بن وائل السهمي سيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account shifts from one arrogant denier to polytheists who take gods besides God, hoping their idols will rescue them from punishment and give them honor.
rows.anchor: وجمع لأن نفي العز عن الواحد قد لا يقتضي نفيه عما زاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking worldly honor from needy servants ends in disgrace: it requires abandoning truth for falsehood, though God may respite the misguided until disgrace is deserved.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى ربما أمهل المخذول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gods will repudiate their worshippers and become their enemies, as the cited verses also describe followers and objects of worship disowning one another.
rows.anchor: فيقع بينهم العداوة كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular word ḍidd with plural pronouns portrays the disbelievers as united in a single bloc, yet their gods turn against them and bring them humiliation.
rows.anchor: ووحد إشارة إلى اتفاق الكلمة بحيث إنهم لفرط تضامنهم كشيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends the fire-born devils against entrenched disbelievers to agitate them violently toward sins and degrading acts they know are ugly, like boiling water or flying sparks.
rows.anchor: أي تحركهم تحريكا شديدا , وتزعجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not hurry their punishment: God counts every breath while granting respite and blessings, then removes them at their appointed term; the delay brings them misery rather than comfort.
rows.anchor: بإمهالنا لهم وإدرارنا النعم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah sequence moves from general blessings in al-Naḥl to blessings for believers and the righteous in al-Isrāʾ, al-Kahf, and Maryam; repeated naming of the Merciful supports this link.
rows.anchor: أتبعت سورة النعم الخاصة بالمؤمنين وبعض العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are gathered to the Merciful as honored delegates arriving swiftly and exaltedly at a king’s court, welcomed with hospitality and dignity.
rows.anchor: كما تقدم الوفود على الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals include those guilty of sins as well as unbelief; they are driven forcefully to Hell, thirsty.
rows.anchor: كالبهائم سوقا عنيفا مزعجا حثيثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither group can grant or receive intercession except one who took a covenant through divinely enabled faith and obedience, on which God promised intercession or its receipt.
rows.anchor: الإيمان والطاعة التي وعده عليها أن يشفع أو أن يشفع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is reciprocal ellipsis: mentioning the Merciful first implies the Avenger later, while mentioning Hell later implies the omitted Paradise first.
rows.anchor: ذكر الرحمن أولا دليلا على المنتقم ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a child would be the closest intercessor, refuting the alleged child of God eliminates the idolaters’ hoped-for private and general intercessors and their source of honor.
rows.anchor: وكان الولد أقرب شفيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi attributes the claimed divine child to the Jews as ʿUzayr, Christians as the Messiah, and polytheists as the angels.
rows.anchor: قالت اليهود : عزير , والنصارى : المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim is a grave, weighty abomination; despite their solidity and distance, the heavens nearly split, the earth opens wide, and the mountains fall quickly as under an unbearable load.
rows.anchor: مع بعدها من أصحاب هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʿaw here means to name or assign; the object of the naming is omitted to make the condemnation of every such attribution universal.
rows.anchor: هذا المفعول الثاني , وحذف الأول لإرادة العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no child and cannot have one: offspring requires shared kind, but nothing shares the absolute Creator’s kind; every heavenly and earthly being comes to him as a subdued servant, which opposes sonship and partnership.
rows.anchor: مسخرا مقهورا خائفا راجيا , فكيف يكون العبد ابنا أو شريكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also supports the rule that a parent and child are both freed if purchased.
rows.anchor: فهي من الدليل على عتق الولد والوالد إذا اشتريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who are audacious against truth are humbled by it, while those humbled before truth gain honor; the author links this to God’s description of believers as humble to believers and mighty against disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أن من تعود الجراءة بالباطل كان ذليلا في الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier generations were stronger, more numerous, and better equipped, yet God destroyed them; only their reports and traces remain.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق إلا سماع أخبارهم , ومشاهدة آثارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close asks whether anyone can perceive them by sight or touch, or hear even a faint sound, and returns to the surah’s theme of mercy for allies and warning for enemies through revelation.
rows.anchor: أي صوتا خفيا فضلا عن أن يكون جليا
